explanation: Zinc is more reactive than hydrogen, so it displaces hydrogen from dilute sulfuric acid, forming zinc sulfate and releasing hydrogen gas.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Grey zinc granules in colourless dilute sulphuric acid.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A colourless zinc sulphate solution; the granules shrink as they're consumed.
beaker_view.observation: Bubbles form on the granules' surface and the test tube warms noticeably to the touch as the reaction proceeds.
